item.title: By: Jennifer Faith Stanley
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Faith Stanley
item.content:encoded:
I am overwhelmed by finding you folks at this moment, exactly what I was asking for. A beautiful stranger on the other side of the world, in a “random” gene keys community cauldron call, lead me to Hospicing Modernity in response to my desire to move deep sadness and layers of ancestral settler guilt.

Thank you for this essential and pertinent collaborative and creative work. The simultaneous invitation to look hard into the deeply layered collective malaise, the crevices created through centuries of our settler privilege, while holding space for coming together in new ways.

I am an aging straight white settler born in what was known to us as Montreal. I climbed the mountain of privilege in what is known to us as downtown Vancouver and now live, re-settled as co-custodian on stolen land in the colonized indigenous town of Axixic Central Mexico.

Our collaborative creative community, la cochera cultural, is intended to live in after us, “gifted” back to the community in perpetuity. We host an annual Festival Michi-cihualli to honor the goddess of this lake and these precious lands.

This work of yours has inspired me to find ways with our team, to deepen to impact of this festival bringing more of our town’s indigenous peoples together with white settlers, national and international and setting ways to move forward each day.

witn deep gratitude, I am anxious to look deeper into your wealth of resources for this decolonizing work we are being called to do.

Jennifer Faith Stanley

co-founder/co-temporary custodian
